note: 17q24.2 deletions often span both PSMD12 and BPTF, and both independent haploinsufficiencies cause neurodevelopmental disorders with microcephaly and dysmorphisms, supporting potential phenotypic compounding.

evidence.text: BPTF haploinsufficiency independently causes syndromic developmental delay, speech delay, dysmorphic features, and postnatal microcephaly, and is located in the 17q24.2 microdeletion region alongside PSMD12.

source.title: Haploinsufficiency of the chromatin remodeler BPTF causes syndromic developmental and speech delay, postnatal microcephaly, and dysmorphic features
source.quote: BPTF variants were found in unrelated individuals aged between 2.1 and 13 years, who manifest variable degrees of developmental delay/intellectual disability (10/10), speech delay (10/10), postnatal microcephaly (7/9), and dysmorphic features (9/10).

evidence.text: Phenotypic analysis of 17q24.2-q24.3 deletions suggests that clinical variability and genotype-phenotype correlations relate to the combined roles of PSMD12 and BPTF.

source.title: Association of 17q24. 2‐q24. 3 deletions with recognizable phenotype and short telomeres
source.quote: Proposed novel genotype-phenotype correlations based on new literature information on the region include the role of PSMD12 and BPTF, the genes recently associated with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders
